# rustinion_group_file_integrity (Resource)

Manages a group's file integrity monitoring. Agents hash the watched files (sha256, owner, permissions, size, modification time), compare them with a baseline and report changes; changes made by the package manager (dpkg, rpm, apk, opkg, pkg, Windows Update, macOS installer) are recognised and never alert, anything else raises a finding until accepted. Destroying this resource turns monitoring off.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The group these settings belong to.

### Optional

- `critical_push` (Boolean) Push an urgent alert when a critical system file (passwd, shadow, sudoers, sshd_config, SSH keys, system binaries, hosts file) changes outside a package update. Default false: other findings only reach the summary email.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Monitor the group's devices. Default true (the resource exists to turn monitoring on).
- `exclusions` (List of String) Patterns never watched (`*` within a folder, `**` any depth). Default none.
- `paths` (List of String) Extra files or folders (a folder is watched recursively; `~/` = every user's home; `*` wildcards in path segments). Default none.
- `realtime` (Boolean) Linux: also rescan within about 30 seconds of a file event (inotify). Default true.
- `scan_minutes` (Number) Minutes between scheduled scans (5 to 1440). Default 30.
- `use_defaults` (Boolean) Watch the built-in list for each OS (Linux: /etc, /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /boot, systemd units, cron, SSH authorized_keys; Windows: System32 drivers and hosts, startup folders, scheduled tasks, core executables; macOS: LaunchDaemons/LaunchAgents, /etc, /usr/bin; FreeBSD/OPNsense/pfSense: /etc, /usr/local/etc, binaries). Default true.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as group_id.
